source: NCERT Class VIII, Resources and Development, Geography Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Agriculture and Farming Systems
points: **Agriculture** = the cultivation of crops and rearing of livestock; also called **primary activity**.
**Agriculture (arable) + Sericulture (silk) + Pisciculture (fish) + Viticulture (grapes) + Horticulture (fruits/veg)**.
Farming depends on **soil, climate (temperature, rainfall), relief** and **technology**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Farming
points: **Subsistence farming** — grown mainly for the farmer's **own family**; may be **intensive** (small plots, much labour) or **primitive/shifting** (slash-and-burn, called jhum/milpa/ladang in different places).
**Commercial farming** — grown for **sale in the market**; large scale, machinery, high inputs.
**Plantation farming** — a single cash crop grown on large estates (e.g. **tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane**).

sections.heading: 3. Major Crops
points: **Rice** — needs high temperature, high humidity and rainfall; grown in China, India, SE Asia.
**Wheat** — needs moderate temperature and rainfall; grown in India (north), USA, Canada, Russia.
**Millets (jowar, bajra, ragi)** — hardy, grow in poor soil.
**Cotton** — needs high temperature, black soil (India's Deccan); a fibre crop.
**Tea and coffee** — beverage crops; tea (Assam, Darjeeling), coffee (Karnataka).

sections.heading: 4. Cropping Seasons (India)
points: **Kharif** — sown with the monsoon (June–July), harvested Sept–Oct (**rice, maize, cotton, bajra**).
**Rabi** — sown in winter (Oct–Dec), harvested spring (**wheat, gram, mustard**).
**Zaid** — short summer season (watermelon, cucumber).
Modern farming uses **HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation, machinery** (the **Green Revolution**).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Farming types: subsistence (own use; intensive/shifting), commercial, plantation.
Shifting cultivation = jhum (NE India), milpa, ladang; slash-and-burn.
Rice = high temp + rainfall; wheat = moderate; cotton = black soil (Deccan).
Plantation crops: tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane.
Kharif (monsoon: rice/cotton), Rabi (winter: wheat/gram), Zaid (summer).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Kharif** crops (rice, cotton) are sown with the **monsoon**; **Rabi** crops (wheat, gram) in **winter**.
**Shifting cultivation** = jhum/slash-and-burn (subsistence farming).
**Plantation** farming = a single cash crop on large estates (tea/coffee/rubber).
**Cotton** grows best on **black (regur) soil**; **rice** needs plentiful water.
